title: Opening and counting Bigard's many recordings
summary: Radio host plays a record and asks Bigard if he recognizes himself; he cannot say how many records he made.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Luthier, right? Right. That's what we'll be listening to on the other side of the news. Thank you.
There we have one called Ready Eddie. Barney Begard, do you recognize that young fellow in clarinet?
Yes, I do. Quite a long time ago. A lot of these things were made that I never recognized until I hear them again. Then it dawned on me, well, I did this thing, sure.
Do you have any idea how many records you may have recorded over the years? Oh, not the faintest idea.

You lost count after 5,000 I bet. Oh, easy. I made them all with Duke, I made some of my own, I made some with Freddie Slight, and I made a lot of them with Louie. And I made a lot of different groups, you know, like on the side, what do you call a sideline, you know, one of those deals. And made a lot of studio recordings.
